answer.rationale: memory_c2 is the memory that would license the tempting move (switch primary to the low-cost vendor, since its quote alone satisfies the 18% mandate), so it is the one most worth auditing: its original record should tell me whether that switch involved this same component, whether the line had volume slack at the time, and whether 'onboarding was quick' was measured over a full delivery cycle or just the first invoices. A cost win recorded under slack conditions does not transfer to a line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and 14 days to contract expiry \u2014 migration there converts a price gain into delivery exposure, which the primary objective explicitly forbids. memory_c4 is the second check because it underwrites my intended action: I want to confirm the renegotiation lever actually moved price and payment terms materially, and not just terms at the margin, before I bet the cycle on it. Intended action is therefore to negotiate with the incumbent using the low-cost quote as a live benchmark \u2014 this is the one move that pursues the mandate while keeping the integration and delivery schedule intact (memory_c1, memory_c6 suggest term length and volume are available concessions). Kept small and guarded: a bounded negotiation with a walk-away point rather than a multi-year lock, so the switch option survives into the next review if the incumbent will not move. Downstream risk flagged: an 18% cut chased on unit price alone can be recovered by the vendor through quality drift, lengthened lead times, or narrowed service scope, none of which show up in the price line but all of which land on a line with no buffer; I want the concession specified as price plus committed lead time and scope, not price alone. Uncertainty preserved: I have not established that the incumbent can reach the mandate, nor that the low-cost vendor's quote holds at our committed volume; if verification shows memory_c2 came from a comparable component under comparable load, add_second_source or a staged switch becomes the better candidate next cycle.
